[1m[35mBERTH[39m[22m
[90m────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────[39m

[1m[34mUSAGE[39m[22m
  [32mberth[39m [36m[anchor <path> [name] [--refresh] [--yes] | close [--infeed <anchor> | --newfeed] [--name <feed>] [--title <text>] [--force] | drop <name> | clear][39m

[1m[34mDESCRIPTION[39m[22m
  Anchor ChRIS paths in this session's berth: download each into the anchors
  folder, list them, return the outgoing folder to ChRIS as one node, drop
  one, or clear them all

[1m[34mOPTIONS[39m[22m
  [1m[37mSUBCOMMANDS:[39m[22m
    [33m(none)[39m                   List the anchors: name, ChRIS path, node or
                             none, files, size, when anchored; and when
                             the berth last closed
    [33manchor <path> [name][39m     Download a ChRIS path you can read into
                             <anchors>/<name>/, named by its last part
                             unless a name is given
      [33m--refresh[39m              Download an anchor that stands again
      [33m--yes, -y[39m              Answer yes to the question above 10 GB
    [33mclose[39m                    Upload the outgoing folder, with berth.json,
                             to ~/berth/<uuid>/ and make it one node
                             (pl-dsdircopy): a child of the node every
                             anchor is under, or a new feed when none is
      [33m--infeed <anchor>[39m      A child of that anchor's node
      [33m--newfeed[39m              A new feed over every anchor
      [33m--name <feed>[39m          The new feed's name
      [33m--title <text>[39m         The node's title (berth work)
      [33m--force, -f[39m            Answer yes when your processes still run
    [33mdrop <name>[39m              Remove one anchor; ChRIS still holds it
    [33mclear[39m                    Remove every anchor and empty the outgoing

                             yet closed

  Under your own ~/feeds an anchor has a node, the plugin instance its
  path runs through, which must be finishedSuccessfully; anywhere else
  (uploads, PACS, /PUBLIC, /SHARED) it has none. Anchors of two nodes,
  or of a node and of none, want --infeed or --newfeed to close. A close
  removes nothing. help anchors says more.

[1m[35mDCM[39m[22m
[90m────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────[39m

[1m[34mUSAGE[39m[22m
  [32mdcm[39m [36m<series|tags> <path> [options][39m

[1m[34mDESCRIPTION[39m[22m
  Read DICOM without leaving the session. `dcm series` answers what a folder
  is as a series: identity, modality, instance count, stack order, geometry,
  transfer syntax, bytes, and any annotations saved for its UID. `dcm tags`
  lists every element of a file, or what a folder's files share against what

[1m[34mDESCRIPTION[39m[22m
  Plays a manifest (a script is one): its lines run in order in a scope of
  their own, each shown as it runs, and the first refused line stops it,

  directory the play began in, so a manifest that cds into a feed does not
  leave every surface there. The manifest is read from the session's
  filesystem first and from the engine's disk second. --status runs nothing:
  each line is expanded as a dry run expands it and its verb says, from what
  the backend keeps and never from the cloud, where it stands (not yet, with
  what is missing; ready; done; changed, with what changed), one row per line
  and a count at the end; a verb that keeps nothing reads as a dash. See
  docs/manifest.adoc.

[1m[35mPROC[39m[22m
[90m────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────[39m

[1m[34mUSAGE[39m[22m
  [32mproc[39m [36m<jobs|stat|feeds|refresh|retry|find|here|watch|unwatch> [args][39m

[1m[34mDESCRIPTION[39m[22m
  /proc/jobs is a job history inspector for every computation visible to the
  current ChRIS identity. Each plugin instance is a discrete job with a
  parent, zero or more children, a status, parameters, and a log. Jobs are
  grouped into feeds (pipeline runs), and the parent-child relationships form
  a DAG: the execution tree of a full computation. /proc/jobs exposes this as
  a navigable filesystem. The daemon restores an identity-scoped local
  topology checkpoint, validates feed visibility with CUBE, and reconciles all
  plugin instances in the background. Restored queries remain usable while
  syncing; a cold cache still guards global queries until complete. CUBE
  remains authoritative.

[1m[34mSUBCOMMANDS[39m[22m
  jobs list                               List all feeds with full counter fields (default 20)
  jobs list --fields id,title,erroredJobs Select columns
  jobs list --sort erroredJobs --reverse  Sort by field
  jobs list --table                       Tabular output
  jobs list --csv                         CSV output
  jobs list --all                         All feeds (no limit)
  jobs list --search failed               Filter by title substring
  jobs list --force                       Wait for warm-up, then list complete results
  jobs inspect                            Show all available field names
  stat                                   Show cache summary
  stat <feed_id>                         Show raw counters + topology state for one feed
  feeds <query> [--fresh] [--force]      Find feeds by title, feed_N name or id; an id the roster lacks is asked of CUBE; --fresh walks the whole feed index now; --force waits for warm-up
  feeds --new                            Feeds shared with you since your last visit, not yet opened (NEW)
  seen <feed ...> | all                  Take the NEW mark off feeds you have looked at
  universe                               Every feed the index holds as it landed: size, status, pipeline shape; honest while warming
  layout <name>                          Where a surface last laid the universe out under a layout, as the session keeps it
  layout put <name> <places>             Keep a layout: node ids to [x, y, z], as JSON (surfaces put what they settle)
  refresh                                Rebuild entire proc cache
  refresh <feed_id>                      Rebuild cache for one feed only
  retry                                  Resume a failed topology sweep at its failed page
  find <id>                              Targeted instance lookup; available during warm-up
  find <name> [--force]                  Name search; --force waits for warm-up
  here                                   Navigate from a CFS feed/output path to its matching job
  jump [--where] <id | name>             Go to a feed or node by id or /proc name (feed_N, plugin_N); a number that is both is not guessed; --where only answers
  watch <feed>                           Keep a running feed live: sample it while it runs, push its DAG to every surface
  watch                                  List the session's watches with their state
